content: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever: Its loveliness increases; it will never pass into nothingness.
author: John Keats
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. True art and creative work are not about clever technique; they demand total emotional skin in the game. When you create safely to please an audience or avoid criticism, the work feels hollow and bloodless.

In John Keats's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Pouring your genuine spirit, vulnerability, and raw lived experience into what you make is what gives it enduring life. The work that resonates across centuries is always the work created with unapologetic personal truth.
reflectionPrompt: How can you welcome mistakes and awkward beginnings as essential steps in your creative evolution?

originalQuote: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever: Its loveliness increases; it will never pass into nothingness; but so it is in the nature of such things to be, that, as we on earth converse with them, they change for the very reason of fond regard.
